# odoo-work-cli entries add

## NAME

odoo-work-cli-entries-add - Create a new timesheet entry

## SYNOPSIS

```text
odoo-work-cli entries add --description TEXT --hours H --project-id ID [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] [--task-id ID] [--json | --format FORMAT]
```

## DESCRIPTION

Create a timesheet entry of --hours on the day --date (default today)
with the description --description, on the project --project-id and,
optionally, its task --task-id.

--hours takes decimal hours (2.5) or H:MM (2:30) and must be greater than
zero. The input is checked before any connection is made.

With --dry-run the input is validated, project and task are resolved
(an unknown project, or a task of another project, is a validation
error), and the entry that would be created is printed; nothing is
written. Entries of the same day with the same project, task and
description are reported as possible duplicates.

## OPTIONS

`--date` *YYYY-MM-DD*
:   Day of the entry, YYYY-MM-DD.

    *string; optional; default: today*

`--description` *TEXT*
:   TEXT describing the work.

    *string; required*

`--dry-run`
:   Validate and print the entry that would be written, without writing it.

    *flag; optional*

`--hours` *H*
:   Hours worked, decimal (2.5) or H:MM (2:30).

    *string; required*

`--project-id` *ID*
:   ID of the project to book on (see projects).

    *integer; required*

`--task-id` *ID*
:   ID of the task to book on (see tasks); must belong to the project.

    *integer; optional*

## GLOBAL OPTIONS

`--format` *FORMAT*
:   Output FORMAT: table, json or jsonl.

    *one of table, json, jsonl; optional; default: table*

`--json`
:   Shorthand for --format json.

    *flag; optional*

`--backend` *BACKEND*
:   BACKEND: odoo or fake (offline, made-up data; env ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND).

    *string; optional; default: odoo; env: ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND*

`--config` *FILE*
:   Read only the config FILE (skip discovery).

    *string; optional*

`-h`, `--help`
:   Print the help of the command and exit.

## OUTPUT

Prints "Created entry ID". With --dry-run, "Dry run: would create this
entry; nothing was written." followed by the entry, and a warning per
possible duplicate.

With --json the created entry. With --dry-run and --json the proposed
entry with id null, dry_run true and duplicates (entry_dry_run.schema.json).

Fields of entry.schema.json:

`id`
:   *integer*

`date`
:   *string (YYYY-MM-DD)*

`project_id`
:   *integer or null*

`project`
:   *string or null*

`task_id`
:   *integer or null*

`task`
:   *string or null*

`description`
:   *string*

`hours`
:   *number*

`minutes`
:   *integer*

`employee`
:   *string or null*

`status`
:   *string or null*

`company`
:   *string or null*

Fields of entry_dry_run.schema.json: those of entry.schema.json, except:

`id`
:   null for add: the entry does not exist yet.

    *integer or null*

`dry_run`
:   *always true*

`duplicates`
:   Entries of the same day with the same project, task and description.

    *array of object (entry.schema.json)*

## ENVIRONMENT

`ODOO_URL`
:   Odoo server URL; overrides url from the config files.

`ODOO_DATABASE`
:   Odoo database name; overrides database.

`ODOO_USERNAME`
:   Odoo login, usually an e-mail address; overrides username.

`ODOO_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo API key, used for XML-RPC. Despite the name, not the login password.

`ODOO_WEB_PASSWORD`
:   Odoo login password, used for the web session of clock in and clock out.

`ODOO_TOTP_SECRET`
:   TOTP secret (base32 or otpauth:// URL) for accounts with two-factor authentication.

`ODOO_OP_TIMEOUT`
:   Timeout of the 1Password call that resolves [op_secrets], a Go duration; default 5s.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_NO_OP`
:   If 1, true, yes or on, [op_secrets] is ignored and the 1Password CLI is never called.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_BACKEND`
:   Backend, odoo (default) or fake; --backend overrides it.

`ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE`
:   State file of the fake backend; default odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json in the temporary directory.

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
:   Base directory of the global config file; default ~/.config.

## FILES

`~/.config/odoo-work-cli/config.toml`
:   Global configuration ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/odoo-work-cli/config.toml if XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set). Created by odoo-work-cli config install.

`.odoo-work-cli.toml`
:   Configuration of a directory tree. Every such file from the filesystem root down to the current directory is merged over the global file, the deepest last. --config FILE loads only FILE instead.

`$TMPDIR/odoo-work-cli-fake-state.json`
:   State of the fake backend (--backend fake); ODOO_WORK_CLI_FAKE_STATE sets another path. Delete it to start over with the seed data.

## EXIT STATUS

0 on success, 1 on any error, including usage errors. With --json or --format json|jsonl the error is printed on standard output as one JSON object, {"error": {"kind": KIND, "message": TEXT}}, and nothing on standard error; otherwise as "Error: TEXT" on standard error, after usage errors followed by the usage.

Error kinds this command can fail with:

`auth`
:   Authentication failed: wrong API key or login password, TOTP rejected.

`validation`
:   Invalid input: unknown flag, bad argument, malformed date, time or hours, a time in the future, an unknown project.

`network`
:   Odoo cannot be reached: DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS.

`config`
:   The local configuration is missing or invalid.

`secrets_locked`
:   1Password is locked or unreachable, so op:// references could not be resolved.

`internal`
:   Anything else: an unexpected Odoo response or a bug.

## EXAMPLES

Preview 90 minutes on a task without writing anything:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli entries add --project-id 1 --task-id 13 --date 2026-04-09 --hours 1:30 --description "Review fuzzy matching" --dry-run
Dry run: would create this entry; nothing was written.
  Date:        2026-04-09
  Project:     Lighthouse Portal (1)
  Task:        Code review (13)
  Hours:       1:30
  Description: Review fuzzy matching
Warning: possible duplicate of entry 4018 (same day, project, task and description)
```

Book 45 minutes:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli entries add --project-id 2 --task-id 22 --date 2026-04-09 --hours 0:45 --description "Answer support mail"
Created entry 5000
```

Book and print the created entry as JSON:

```console
$ odoo-work-cli entries add --project-id 3 --task-id 31 --date 2026-04-09 --hours 0.5 --description "Standup" --json
{
  "id": 5001,
  "date": "2026-04-09",
  "project_id": 3,
  "project": "Internal",
  "task_id": 31,
  "task": "Meetings",
  "description": "Standup",
  "hours": 0.5,
  "minutes": 30,
  "employee": "Alex Demo",
  "status": "draft",
  "company": "Example Consulting"
}
```
